questions.question: A new agent opens Incident > All and sees rows and columns of incident data. How should they interpret this screen?

options.text: A form showing one incident record and its fields
A list of incident records, with one field per column
A report of incident counts, with one group per column
A view definition, with one form section per column

explanation.correct: This screen is a list. ServiceNow documentation describes a list as displaying a set of records from a table, and states that each column in a list corresponds to a field on the table, so each row the agent sees is one incident record and each column is one Incident field. Users can search, sort, filter, and edit data directly in the list. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/c_UseLists.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: A form displays information from one record in a table. Seeing many incident rows at once means this is a list, not the form of a single record.
Counting records per group is what a grouped list or a report does. A plain list shows the individual records, one per row, rather than aggregated counts.
A view defines which elements appear when a list or form opens, but it is not shown as a grid of form sections; the columns here are table fields.

course.moduleTitle: SNAF Module 3: Configure applications for business

source.excerpt: A list shows records from a table. On the ServiceNow platform, lists can be interacted with in various ways. In both the core platform and workspace, each row is a record and each column is a field.

questions.question: An agent opens an incident from a link whose URL sets sysparm_view to another view. Yesterday, the agent switched the Incident form to the Mobile view. Which view does the form open in?

options.text: The view named in the link's URL
The Mobile view saved as a preference
The Default view for the Incident table
The view their assignment group last used

explanation.correct: When a user switches views, the selected view is saved as a user preference so the user sees the same view by default when the form opens. The documentation states that if a user has a view saved as a preference and opens a URL that specifies another view, the form displays in the view saved in the user preference, not the URL. Setting the sysparm_view_forced parameter to true overrides this behavior. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/view-management-overview.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The sysparm_view parameter can be overwritten by a user's stored view preference, so the URL's view is not used unless sysparm_view_forced is set to true.
The form does not fall back to the Default view. The agent's saved preference (Mobile) is what the form opens in.
The selected view is saved as the individual user's preference. The documentation does not describe group-level view preferences deciding which view opens.

course.moduleTitle: SNAF Module 3: Configure applications for business

source.excerpt: Views allow users to display lists or forms in different ways. System administrators can create views for different user types, such as employee, self-service, and mobile users.

questions.question: An administrator wants the Incident list to show the company of the user in the Assigned to field, without adding a new field to the Incident table. What makes this possible?

options.text: A related list of the assigned user's records
Dot-walking through the Assigned to field
A reference qualifier on the Assigned to field
A template that copies the user's company

explanation.correct: Dot-walking provides access to fields on related tables from a form, list, or script. If the current table contains a reference to another table, any field on the referenced table can be accessed using dot-walking. The documentation's own example, incident.assigned_to.company, references the company of the user assigned to an incident. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/c_DotWalking.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Related lists appear on forms and show records in other tables that are related to the current record. They do not add a column with a referenced user's company to the Incident list.

Reference qualifiers filter the data that is returned for a reference field, such as only active users in the Assigned to lookup. They do not display fields from the referenced User record in the list.
Templates populate fields when records are submitted, so the company would need its own field on Incident. Dot-walking reads the value directly from the referenced User record.

course.moduleTitle: SNAF Module 3: Configure applications for business

source.excerpt: Dot-walking collects data from related tables via reference fields. It works in form layout, but not in form design.

questions.question: In the Incident filter, an agent sees a greater than operator for Priority, but not for Active. What decides which operators the condition builder offers?

options.text: The type of the field selected
The roles the agent has been given
The list view the agent is using
The AND or OR grouping in the filter

explanation.correct: A condition has three parts: field, operator, and value. The operator is a choice list based on the field type. The documentation uses this exact example: on the Incident table, the greater than operator does not apply to the Active field, but it does apply to the Priority field. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/c_ConditionBuilder.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: User access rights shape the Field choice list, not the operators. Operators are based on the field type.
The operator choice list is based on the field type. The list view in use does not change it.
AND and OR group condition lines together. They do not decide which operators a field offers.

course.moduleTitle: SNAF Module 3: Configure applications for business

source.excerpt: A filter condition has three parts. Field-- able to be chosen based on user access, can include related tables. Operator-- varies by field type. Value-- text entry or choice list based on field.

questions.question: An agent wants the Business service column on their own Incident list, but their teammates' lists must stay exactly as they are. What should the agent use?

options.text: Configure > List Layout from a column heading
The personalize list icon to choose their columns
A new list view created from the List Layout slushbucket
A Group By on the Business service column heading

explanation.correct: Personal lists let a user choose which columns appear and in what order for a specific list view, based on individual preferences. ServiceNow documentation states that personal list customizations do not affect what other users see, and the agent opens them with the personalize list icon in the corner of the list. This meets the goal without changing the shared layout. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/c_PersonalLists.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Configure > List Layout changes the columns of the list view itself, the layout every user of that view receives, so teammates would also see the new column.
Creating views requires the admin role and is done from List Layout, so it is not an agent's personal setting. A view is a named layout other users can switch to, not a personal preference.
Group By aggregates the list by a field and shows a record count per group. It organizes records but does not add a column to the list.

course.moduleTitle: SNAF Module 3: Configure applications for business

source.excerpt: Where the list layout configuration affects everyone, the personalize list modifies the layout of a list for an individual user. It does not affect the platform default.

questions.question: An agent personalized the columns of their Incident list. Later, an administrator adds the Configuration item column to that list view with Configure > List Layout. What will the agent see?

options.text: It appears in their personal list at once
It appears once they reset to column defaults
Their personal list is replaced by the new layout
It appears the next time they log in again

explanation.correct: The list layout documentation notes that if you use personal lists and then the list view is configured differently, the changes do not appear until you reset your personal list to column defaults. Resetting is done from the personalize list icon with the Reset to column defaults button. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/list-administration/t_ConfigureTheListLayout.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: A personal list keeps the agent's own column choices. The administrator's new column does not appear until the agent resets to column defaults.
The personal list is not replaced. It stays as the agent set it until the agent resets it to column defaults.
Logging in again does not apply the change. The column appears only after the agent resets the personal list to column defaults.

course.moduleTitle: SNAF Module 3: Configure applications for business

source.excerpt: Any global changes that occur at the system level will not be reflected in a personalized list. If the system administrator configures a list view a user has personalized, they will not see those newly added default changes until they choose reset to column defaults.

questions.question: An agent has unsaved edits on an existing incident and switches the form to a different view. What happens to the edits?

options.text: They are discarded when the new view loads
They are held as a draft until the next save
The form is submitted and the edits saved
A prompt asks the agent to confirm leaving

explanation.correct: Switching views submits the form, which saves all changes and triggers any onSubmit client scripts that apply. For the same reason, you cannot switch form views on a new form that has not been saved yet. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/view-management-overview.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The edits are not discarded. Switching views submits the form and saves all changes.
No draft is kept. Switching views submits the form immediately, so the changes are saved at that point.
The leave-page confirmation applies when you navigate away from a form without saving. Switching views instead submits and saves the form.

course.moduleTitle: SNAF Module 3: Configure applications for business

source.excerpt: The view name will appear in brackets beside the table or form title, unless it's the default view.

questions.question: An agent selects an incident number in the Incident list, and a page opens showing fields, form sections, and related lists for that incident. What is this page?

options.text: A list showing records from several related tables
A form showing the data of that incident record
A report summarizing that incident's field values
A dashboard showing the Incident table's settings

explanation.correct: The page is a form. ServiceNow documentation states that a form displays information from one record in a data table, and that users can view and edit records in forms. Fields, sections, and related lists are all listed as form elements; the related lists only show records from other tables that relate to this one incident. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/c_UsingForms.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Although related lists appear at the bottom of the form, the page itself presents one incident record. A list is the view that shows a set of records from a table.
Forms are not reports that summarize data: the documentation says users can view and edit records in forms, and they save changes with Submit, Update, or Save.
The form displays data stored in the selected record, not table configuration. Administrators change the form's contents through form configuration, not by viewing a record.

course.moduleTitle: SNAF Module 3: Configure applications for business

source.excerpt: Forms in ServiceNow show information from a single record in a table, and can be accessed through global search or lists.

questions.question: A new agent is learning the parts of a classic Incident form. Which two descriptions of form elements are correct? (Choose two)

options.text: Sections group related information on the form
The form header stores specific data about the record
Related lists show records in other related tables
Embedded lists save each change as soon as it is made

explanation.correct: The forms documentation describes sections as grouping related information on the form, and related lists as displaying records in other tables that have relationships to the current record. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/c_UsingForms.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Fields store specific data about the record. The form header provides navigation tools and actions related to the record.
Changes to embedded lists are saved when the form is saved, not as each change is made.

course.moduleTitle: SNAF Module 3: Configure applications for business

source.excerpt: Forms include fields, sections, formatters, UI actions, and related lists. These elements enhance how users navigate and interact with forms.

questions.question: An agent edits several fields on an incident form and then opens a different module without saving. The instance uses default form settings. What happens?

options.text: The changes are saved automatically as a draft
A message asks them to confirm leaving the page
The changes are discarded with no message shown
The form locks editing until the record is saved

explanation.correct: Navigating away from a form without saving is how a user cancels changes. ServiceNow documentation says that when a confirmation message appears, the user selects Leave this Page to confirm the cancellation, and that administrators can turn this message off by setting glide.ui.dirty_form_support to false. With default settings, the agent is warned before the unsaved edits are lost. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/t_EditingInForms.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Changes are kept only when the record is saved with Submit, Update, or Save. Navigating away without saving cancels the changes; it does not store a draft.
The changes are discarded only after the user confirms. The silent behavior happens only if an administrator disables the message with glide.ui.dirty_form_support.
Nothing in the documented form editing behavior locks the record. The user either confirms leaving the page or stays on the form to keep editing and save.

course.moduleTitle: SNAF Module 3: Configure applications for business

source.excerpt: Changing views will prompt you to save or discard changes before reloading the form.

questions.question: An administrator wants an existing related list to appear at the bottom of the Problem form for all users. Which form context menu option should they use?

options.text: Configure > List Layout
Configure > Related Lists
Switch Views to Advanced
Create Favorite on the form

explanation.correct: To add a related list to a form, select the form context menu icon and then Configure > Related Lists, move the related list from the Available list to the Related list, and save. Related lists appear at the bottom of the form. Form configuration covers both the form layout and the related list layout, which changes which related lists appear at the bottom of the form. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/configure-form-layout.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Configure > List Layout chooses the columns shown in a list view. It does not add related lists to a form.
Switching views changes which existing view you see and saves it as your preference. It does not add a related list to the form.
Create Favorite adds the list or record to your Favorites menu. It does not change the form's related lists.

course.moduleTitle: SNAF Module 3: Configure applications for business

source.excerpt: There are several ways to modify a form-- Form Builder, Form Design, and Form Layout.

questions.question: Service desk agents type the same category, subcategory, and assignment group on every password reset incident. An administrator wants them to fill these fields in one step. What should the administrator provide?

options.text: A new table that extends Incident for resets
A form template storing those field values
A list view filtered to reset incidents
A scheduled report of past reset incidents

explanation.correct: Form templates exist to simplify submitting new records by populating fields automatically. The documented approach is to fill in the most-used fields for a table, save them as a template, and make the template available to users, who can then apply it when creating a record (for example from the template bar). See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_Templates.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Extending the Incident table creates a new table structure; it does not supply default values for the fields agents fill in on each new incident.
A list view controls which fields appear when the list opens. It helps agents find existing records but does not prefill fields on a new one.
Reports summarize and display existing data. A scheduled report of past incidents gives no way to populate fields on a record being created.

course.moduleTitle: SNAF Module 3: Configure applications for business

source.excerpt: To use a template, fill in the most common fields for a table. Save it as a template, and make it available to users. Users can apply templates manually when creating records, or administrators can set scripts to apply them automatically.

questions.question: An administrator wants a template applied automatically whenever a user creates a new record on the Windows Server [cmdb_ci_win_server] table. How should the template be set up?

options.text: Give it the table's name, cmdb_ci_win_server
Add every user group to the Groups field on it
Run it from a scheduled job on the table
Add a module that opens a form with it

explanation.correct: To make a template apply automatically to new, user-created records on a table, set the template name to match the name of that table. The documentation uses this exact example: Name set to cmdb_ci_win_server and Table set to Windows Server [cmdb_ci_win_server]. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_Templates.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Automatic templates are always global and do not honor the User and Groups fields, so filling in groups does not make a template apply automatically.
A scheduled job creates new records from a template on a schedule. It does not apply the template to records that users create.
A template module opens a form with pre-populated template data when someone selects it. It does not apply to every new record automatically.

course.moduleTitle: SNAF Module 3: Configure applications for business

source.excerpt: Only certain groups should create templates to avoid bypassing processes, like mandatory fields and UI policies, particularly for records using condition based flows or workflows.

questions.question: An agent hid several fields on the Incident form with the personalize form icon and now wants the standard form back. What should the agent do?

options.text: Personalize the form again and select Reset
Select Reset to column defaults on the form
Navigate away and then reopen the incident
Expand any form sections that are collapsed

explanation.correct: To restore the default form view after personalizing, personalize the form and click Reset. The hidden fields stay hidden across visits: the documentation notes that if you navigate away, the next time you personalize the form you must reset your customizations to show fields that you hid. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/t_PersonalizeAForm.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Reset to column defaults belongs to the personalize list icon on lists. Forms are restored with the Reset option in the Personalize Form menu.

Navigating away does not undo the personalization. The documentation says that if you navigate away from the form, the next time you personalize the form you must reset your customizations to show fields that you have hidden.

Collapsing or expanding a form section is a separate preference that only shows or hides a whole section. Fields hidden with the personalize form icon come back only when the agent personalizes the form and selects Reset.

course.moduleTitle: SNAF Module 3: Configure applications for business

source.excerpt: The personalized form will remain each time the user logs in. Only fields configured to display are available in the personalize form menu.

questions.question: An administrator opens the Policies and rules tab in Table Builder for a custom table. Which two sections on that tab are read-only there, with links to manage them elsewhere on the platform? (Choose two)

options.text: UI Policies
Business Rules
Client Scripts
Transform Maps

explanation.correct: The Policies and rules tab has several sections, but only UI policies can be edited within Table Builder. The other sections, including Business Rules and Client Scripts (as well as Access control rules and Workspace view rules), are read-only and contain links to manage their content in other parts of the platform. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/form-builder-glide-family-release/form-builder-policies-rules.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: UI Policies is the one section you can edit within Table Builder, so it is not read-only.
Transform Maps is not a section of the Policies and rules tab. The tab covers UI Policies, Access control rules, Client Scripts, Business Rules, and Workspace view rules.

course.moduleTitle: SNAF Module 3: Configure applications for business

source.excerpt: In the policies and rules section, administrators can configure UI policies, access control rules, client scripts, business rules, workspace view rules.

questions.question: An agent filtering the Incident list wants a condition on the caller's company, but the field menu shows only Incident fields. What should the agent select first?

options.text: Show Related Fields in the field list
Group By on the Caller column heading
Configure > List Layout from a heading
Show Matching on a Caller cell value

explanation.correct: To dot-walk in a condition builder, you first select Show Related Fields on the fields menu, which lets you add fields from related tables to the query. The documentation uses this exact case: filtering the Incident table by the company of the caller by selecting Company under Caller > User fields, which becomes Caller.Company. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/dot-walking-examples.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Group By aggregates the list by a field and shows a count per group. It does not add fields from the caller's User record to the filter's field menu.
Configure > List Layout chooses which columns appear in the list. It does not change the fields offered in the condition builder.
Show Matching is a quick filter on the field value you right-click, which here is the caller, not the caller's company. Conditions on related fields need Show Related Fields.

questions.question: Several agents have personal lists for a list view. When an administrator removes an inactive field from that admin-configured default view, what happens to their personal lists?

options.text: They keep the field until agents remove it
They reset to follow the default view
They are deleted along with the field
They stay as is until agents reset them

explanation.correct: The personal lists documentation states that if an inactive field is removed from an admin-configured default view, any personal lists reset to follow the default view, which removes the inactive field from the personal list. This is an exception to the usual rule that layout changes appear only after a user resets to column defaults. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/c_PersonalLists.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: In this case the agents do not have to act. Removing an inactive field from the default view resets personal lists to follow the default view.
The personal lists are not deleted. They reset to follow the default view, without the inactive field.
Existing personal lists do change. They reset to follow the default view when the inactive field is removed, without any action from the agents.

questions.question: An administrator needs to change which fields appear on the Incident form for all users. Which three tools can they use for this? (Choose 3)

options.text: Form Builder
Form Designer
Form Layout
List Layout

explanation.correct: Form Layout changes which fields are visible on a form. Form Designer accomplishes the same tasks as Form Layout in a graphical tool, though since the Australia release it is being prepared for future deprecation. Form Builder has all of the Form Designer and Form Layout options, and the documentation recommends trying it first. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/configure-form-layout.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: List Layout configures which columns appear in a list and creates list views. It does not change the fields on a form.

questions.question: An agent wants to hide a few non-mandatory fields on the Incident form for themselves only, leaving colleagues' forms unchanged. What should the agent use?

options.text: Configure > Form Builder
Configure > Form Layout
The personalize form icon
A UI policy on the Incident table

explanation.correct: With form personalization, users can choose which fields appear on a specific form view according to their own preferences. Personal form customizations do not affect what other users see on their forms. Users open the Personalize Form menu from the personalize form icon in the form header and clear the check box for each field they want to hide. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/t_PersonalizeAForm.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Form Builder configures the form itself, so its changes apply to everyone who uses that form view.
Configuring the form layout changes the form for all users. The documentation says to configure the form when changes must be visible to all users.
UI policies change how forms appear, for example hiding fields based on role or input, for every user they apply to. They are not one agent's personal preference.

questions.question: An agent must set the same Assignment group on 15 incidents shown in a list. According to the documentation, which approach is the quickest?

options.text: Open each incident form and update it
Select cells and use the list editor
Apply a template to each of the incidents
Personalize the list to show the field

explanation.correct: You can edit multiple records at the same time using the list editor. The documentation states that if you want to update a single field on multiple records to have the same value, the list editor is the quickest method. Select the cells with Shift or Ctrl, open the list editor, enter the value, and save. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/t_EditMultRecUsingListEditor.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Editing each form works, but the list editor lets you edit field values directly from a list without opening a form, and it is the documented quickest method for this task.
Templates populate fields to simplify submitting new records. They are not the documented way to update one field across many existing records.
Personalizing a list changes which columns appear and their order. It does not change any field values.

questions.question: In Configure > Form Layout, an administrator wants to add a field from the caller's User record to the Incident form. How are related tables like Caller marked in the Available list?

options.text: Shown in green, followed by a plus (+)
Shown in bold, followed by a right arrow (>)
Shown in red, marked with an asterisk (*)
Shown in gray, wrapped in brackets ([ ])

explanation.correct: In Form Layout, available items that appear in green followed by a plus (+) sign represent related tables, and you use dot-walking to access their fields. The dot-walking documentation adds that when such a reference field is highlighted, an expand icon appears, and a field added from it shows its full dot-walked name, for example Assigned to.Active. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/configure-form-layout.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Related tables in the Available list are shown in green with a plus (+) sign, not in bold with an arrow.
Related tables are shown in green with a plus (+) sign. An asterisk is not how Form Layout marks dot-walkable fields.
Related tables are shown in green with a plus (+) sign, not in gray brackets.

questions.question: The Assigned to lookup on a custom form lists every user, including inactive ones. The administrator wants only active users offered in that field. What should they configure?

options.text: A reference qualifier on the field
An ACL on the User [sys_user] table
A view rule on the custom table
A UI policy that hides the field

explanation.correct: Reference qualifiers filter the data returned for a reference field. Without one, all values in the referenced table appear in the lookup, including inactive users. Creating a reference qualifier returns only the desired values, such as only the active users. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_ReferenceQualifiers.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: ACLs restrict what data specific users can access. The goal here is to filter the values offered in one reference field, which is what a reference qualifier does.
A view rule decides which view a form or list is displayed in. It does not filter the records offered in a reference field.
Hiding the field removes it from the form, but it does not filter which users the lookup offers.

course.moduleTitle: CSA Expansion

questions.question: In Next Experience, an administrator wants to jump straight to the list of System Properties [sys_properties] records from the Unified Navigation. What should they enter, and where?

options.text: sys_properties.list in the Filter field
sys_properties.do in the Filter field
sys_properties.list in the Global search field
sys_properties.do in the Global search field

explanation.correct: The Unified Navigation Filter field lets you quickly navigate to a module. For a list view, you enter the table name in the format name.list, for example sys_properties.list. For a form view, you use name.do instead. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/using-the-next-experience-global-header.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The name.do format in the Filter field opens a form view, not the list of records.
The Global search field searches for a string across the instance. The name.list shortcut is typed in the Filter field.
Global search looks for a string across the instance, and name.do is the form format anyway. Neither opens the list.

course.moduleTitle: CSA Expansion

questions.question: A problem manager working in a List v3 Problem list wants only problems that have three or more related incidents. Which filter feature should they use?

options.text: Dot-walking with Show Related Fields
Related Lists Conditions in the filter
A reference qualifier on the Problem field
A view rule on the Problem table

explanation.correct: Related list conditions let you include a relationship with another table in the filter, and they are supported in List v3. The List v3 filter has a section for current-table conditions and one for related lists conditions. Choosing Incident>Problem with the quantifier Greater Than Or Equal To and a value of 3 returns problems with three or more related incidents. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/create-related-list-query.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Dot-walking reaches fields on a table referenced by the current record. It cannot count how many incident records are related to each problem.
A reference qualifier filters the records offered in a reference field's lookup. It does not filter the Problem list.
A view rule controls which view a form or list is shown in. It does not decide which records the list contains.

course.moduleTitle: CSA Expansion

questions.question: An administrator wants Incident records with Priority 1 - Critical to open in a special Major view, whatever view each agent has saved as a preference. What should they create?

options.text: A view rule with a Priority condition
A UI policy that runs when Priority is 1
A template that sets Priority to 1
Personalized forms for each agent

explanation.correct: A user's chosen view is normally saved as a preference, but a view rule overrides this to force a specified view. Administrators create view rules (System UI > View Rules) with conditions that determine when the system displays a form or list in a specified view. Here, the condition is Priority is 1 - Critical and the view is Major. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/view-management-overview.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: UI policies change how fields behave on a form, for example making them read-only, required, or hidden. They do not choose which view the form opens in.
A template populates field values on new records. It does not control which view a record is displayed in.
Form personalization changes the fields one user sees on a form view. It cannot force a different view based on a field value.

course.moduleTitle: CSA Expansion

questions.question: In the Incident list, an agent double-clicks the Category cell, and the editor that opens also shows the Subcategory field. Why?

options.text: Double click to edit is selected for the list
Subcategory is dependent on Category
The list is set to save data by rows
Enable list edit is selected for the list

explanation.correct: When a field has a dependency relationship, such as Category and Subcategory, the list editor opens a composite editor so that all dependent fields can be edited together. You must have permission to edit all of the dependent fields to use the list editor. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/t_UseTheListEditor.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The Double click to edit option only sets whether the list editor opens with a double-click or a single select. It does not add other fields to the editor.
Saving by rows controls when edits are saved as you move between fields. It does not add dependent fields to the editor.
The Enable list edit option only allows the list editor to open for the list. The extra Subcategory field appears because a dependency relationship opens a composite editor.

course.moduleTitle: CSA Expansion

questions.question: While viewing a page in Next Experience, an agent selects the star icon in the contextual app pill. Where is that page added?

options.text: To the Favorites menu
To the Workspaces menu
To the Admin menu
To the Notifications menu

explanation.correct: Selecting the star icon in the contextual app pill adds the displayed page as a favorite. Favorites appear in the Favorites menu in the Next Experience Unified Navigation, where you can edit their names, icons, colors, and folder groups. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/managing-your-favorites.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The Workspaces menu lists the workspaces you can access. Favorites are not added there.
The Admin menu gives access to items specific to admin functions. Starred pages go to the Favorites menu.
The Notifications menu shows notifications that apply to you. Starring a page adds it to the Favorites menu.

questions.question: A team lead wants the Incident list to show only incidents assigned to their group that are also in the In Progress state. How should the two filter conditions be combined?

options.text: Join them with an OR connector
Join them with an AND connector
Put State under related list conditions
Run each condition as its own filter

explanation.correct: Each condition line is grouped with either an AND or OR connector. The filter requires all condition lines linked with an AND connector to be met, so only incidents that match both the assignment group and the In Progress state are listed. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/c_Filters.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The filter evaluates each OR line separately, so it would also return incidents that match only one of the two conditions.
Related list conditions add a relationship with another table. State is a field on the Incident table itself.
A filter returns the records that meet its own conditions, so two separate filters each list a different set of records. Joining the lines with AND is what requires both conditions.

course.moduleTitle: CSA Expansion

questions.question: An administrator wants a shorter Incident form that shows only a few metrics fields, while agents keep the Default form unchanged. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Create a new view and use Form Layout to pick its fields
Remove the extra fields from the Default view in Form Layout
Use the personalize list icon to hide the extra fields
Add a form section and collapse it for other users

explanation.correct: A view defines the elements that appear when a user opens a form or list, so a separate view can show a smaller subset of fields while the Default view stays the same. Administrators create a view from Configure > Form Layout by basing it on an existing view and then choosing the fields for that view. The documentation even uses the Incident form shown in a Metrics view as an example. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/view-management-overview.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Editing the Default view in Form Layout changes the form every user of that view sees, so the agents' Default form would lose those fields as well.
The personalize list icon changes one user's column choices on a list. It does not configure which fields appear on the Incident form for a group of users.
Sections group fields, but collapsing a section is saved as each user's own preference, so an administrator cannot use it to define a shorter form for others.

questions.question: A service desk manager wants the Incident list organized by Assignment group, with a record count shown for each group. What should they do from the list's column heading?

options.text: Right-click the column and select Sort (a to z)
Right-click the column name and select Group By
Right-click and select Configure > List Layout
Right-click a value and select Show Matching

explanation.correct: Grouping aggregates a list by a field and displays the record count per group. ServiceNow documentation lists right-clicking the column name and selecting Group By as one way to group a list (Ungroup removes it). Each group is named after a field value, here an assignment group, and the count appears next to the group name. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/c_GroupedLists.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Sort (a to z) orders the records by that column in ascending order. The records stay in one list and no per-group record counts are shown.
Configure > List Layout changes which columns appear in the list view and their order. It does not aggregate records or show counts per group.
Show Matching is a quick filter that limits the list to records with the selected value. It narrows the list to one group instead of organizing all of them.

questions.question: An administrator is creating a new Incident form view from Configure > Form Layout. Which view name will the instance accept?

options.text: Field Ops
field-ops
field_ops
field.ops

explanation.correct: When creating a view, the documentation says view names should be unique and cannot use special characters or spaces, only the characters A-Z, a-z, 0-9 and _. Only field_ops uses nothing but letters and an underscore. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/create-delete-view.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: This name contains a space. View names cannot use spaces.
The hyphen is a special character. View names may use only A-Z, a-z, 0-9 and _.
The period is a special character. View names may use only A-Z, a-z, 0-9 and _.

questions.question: An agent sees the breadcrumbs All > Active = true > Category = Software > Priority = 2 on the Incident list and wants to drop only the Category condition. What should they select?

options.text: The Category = Software breadcrumb
The separator (>) before Category = Software
The All breadcrumb at the start of the trail
The Priority = 2 breadcrumb at the end

explanation.correct: Breadcrumbs show the current filter as a hierarchy, from the most general condition on the left to the most specific on the right. According to ServiceNow documentation, selecting the condition separator (>) before a condition removes only that condition, so the list keeps Active = true and Priority = 2 and drops Category = Software. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/c_UsingFiltersAndBreadcrumbs.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Selecting a breadcrumb removes every condition to its right. Choosing Category = Software would drop Priority = 2 and keep the Category condition.
Selecting All removes every condition and returns all incidents in the system, so the Active and Priority conditions would also be lost.
Priority = 2 is the last breadcrumb, so nothing sits to its right; selecting it only refreshes the list and leaves the Category condition in place.

questions.question: An agent opens the personalize list dialog on the Incident list. Which three actions can they take from there? (Choose 3)

options.text: Choose which columns appear and their order
Turn on Compact rows to condense spacing
Create a new field on the underlying table
Reset the list to its column defaults
Create a new list view for other users

explanation.correct: From the personalize list icon, users select the columns and their order, set display options such as the Compact rows check box, and can select the Reset to column defaults button to return to the default layout. These personal changes don't affect what other users see in their lists. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/c_PersonalLists.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Creating fields on the table is part of Configure > List Layout, not the personalize list icon.
Views are created through Configure > List Layout (or Form Layout) by administrators. Personal lists change only the user's own list.

questions.question:
A team lead asks new agents to evaluate these statements about personal and system-wide changes:
A) Personalizing a list does not change what other users see in their lists
B) Configuring a form makes the changes visible to all users
C) Personalizing a form lets a user hide mandatory fields

options.text: A and B are true; C is false
A and C are true; B is false
B and C are true; A is false
A is true; B and C are false

explanation.correct: A is true: personal list customizations don't affect what other users see in their lists. B is true: to make changes to a form that are visible to all users, you must configure the form. C is false: unlike configuring a form, personalizing a form does not let users hide mandatory fields. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/t_PersonalizeAForm.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: C is false, because personalizing a form cannot hide mandatory fields. B is true, because configuring a form is how changes are made visible to all users.
A is true, because personal list customizations don't affect other users. C is false, because personalization cannot hide mandatory fields.
B is also true. Configuring a form, unlike personalizing it, makes the changes visible to all users.

questions.question: An administrator adds items to a related list using a list collector (slushbucket). Which of the following is NOT a feature of the list collector interface?

options.text: An Available column listing items that can be added
A Selected column listing items already chosen
Add and remove icons that move items between columns
A drag-and-drop canvas for placing fields on a form

explanation.correct: The documented list collector interface has two columns, available items on the left and selected items on the right, with add (>) and remove (<) icons, double-click to move items, and in some cases search, filter, and up/down ordering controls. A drag-and-drop canvas for placing fields on a form is not part of it; that kind of visual layout belongs to form design tools. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/t_UseSlushbuckets.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The documentation states that the list collector shows the available items in a column on the left, from which the administrator picks items to add.
The selected items appear in the right-hand column, and new items are added to the bottom of that column, so this is a standard part of the interface.
Items move with the add icon (>) and the remove icon (<), or by double-clicking, so these icons are a documented list collector feature.
